title: Representable slice morphism equals the localized ringed-site morphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], each having finite limits and subcanonical: every $h_W=\operatorname{Hom}(-,W)$ is a sheaf of sets. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits and coverings, with geometric inverse image $L\dashv u^s$, $(u^sF)(W)=F(uW)$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Let $R$ on $\mathcal C$ and $S$ on $\mathcal D$ be sheaves of commutative rings and $c:LR\to S$ a ring map, so that $f=(L\dashv u^s,c):(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ is a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix $V\in\mathcal C$, and let $c_V:Lh_V\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{uV}$ be the isomorphism adjunct to $\beta_V:h_V\to u^sh_{uV}$, $\beta_V(W)(a)=u(a)$ [lem-pur-site-representable-algebraic-pullback].

Two ringed morphisms are attached to $V$. (a) The slice morphism $f_{h_V}:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)/Lh_V,S_{Lh_V})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/h_V,R_{h_V})$, with the slices and restricted rings of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], whose inverse image sends $(H\xrightarrow{\varphi}h_V)$ to $(LH\xrightarrow{L\varphi}Lh_V)$ and whose structural ring map is the restriction of $c$ to the slice over $Lh_V$. (b) The localized ringed-site morphism $f_V:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D/uV),S|_{uV})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/V),R|_V)$ defined by $u_V:(W\to V)\mapsto(uW\to uV)$, with structural map $(f_V)^{-1}(R|_V)\cong(LR)|_{uV}\xrightarrow{c|_{uV}}S|_{uV}$ and restriction comparison $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}\cong j_{uV}^{-1}L$ [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism, def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

Identify $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/V)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/h_V$ and $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D/uV)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)/h_{uV}$ by the equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] (the representables are already sheaves), and $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)/Lh_V\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)/h_{uV}$ by composing structure maps with $c_V$. Under these identifications there is a canonical isomorphism
$$(f_V)^{-1}(H\xrightarrow{\varphi}h_V)\cong(LH\xrightarrow{c_V\circ L\varphi}h_{uV}),$$
natural in $(H,\varphi)$; on the restriction $(G\times h_V\to h_V)$ of a sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C$ it is the comparison $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}G\cong j_{uV}^{-1}LG$ followed by the finite-limit comparison $L(G\times h_V)\cong LG\times Lh_V$ and $c_V$. Under it the restricted rings $R|_V,S|_{uV}$ correspond to $R_{h_V},S_{Lh_V}$, and the structural ring map of $f_V$ corresponds to that of $f_{h_V}$. Hence $f_V$ and $f_{h_V}$ are identified as morphisms of ringed topoi, not only of topoi: their module pullbacks correspond, compatibly with the two restriction comparisons with $f^*$.

Its topology agrees with the element topology via the projection. Use element_site_descent for that topology identity.
